title: Launch two blocks
caption: The host launches two blocks of thirty-two GPU threads. The arrays have thirty-three elements, so some threads have no element to write.

title: Find each thread’s index
caption: Each thread calculates its global index. In block one, thread zero gets thirty-two. The next thread gets thirty-three.

title: Predict which thread writes
caption: The bounds check compares each index with thirty-three. Which of these two threads enters the if block?

title: Only the valid index writes
caption: Thread zero writes ninety-nine at index thirty-two. Thread one skips the assignment because index thirty-three is outside the arrays.

title: Start with a global index
caption: The host launches sixteen threads for thirty-five elements. Block zero, thread three starts at global index three.

title: Calculate the stride
caption: The stride equals the total number of threads. Here, two blocks times eight threads gives a stride of sixteen.

title: Predict this thread’s indices
caption: Starting at three, add sixteen for each visit. Which indices will this thread process before it reaches thirty-five?

title: Visit two array elements
caption: The thread visits indices three and nineteen. Thirty-five is outside the loop, so it stops. At each visit, the thread doubles the input into the output.

title: Copy the inputs to GPU memory
caption: The host copies the two input arrays to GPU memory. Each array contains thirty-three float thirty-two values, and each value occupies four bytes.

title: Allocate and run on the GPU
caption: The host allocates the output on the GPU. Each active GPU thread reads one value from each input and writes one output.

title: Predict the bytes transferred
caption: The result comes back to the CPU. Two arrays went to the GPU, and one returns. How many bytes cross between them?

title: Count the three copies
caption: Each copy moves one hundred thirty-two bytes. Together, the three copies move three hundred ninety-six bytes.

title: Alternating signs split each warp
caption: Each block contains one warp of thirty-two threads. With alternating signs, neighboring lanes take different paths through the kernel.

title: Predict the negative lanes
caption: Look at block zero. How many lanes will take the negative path?

title: Sixteen lanes take each path
caption: Sixteen lanes take the negative path and sixteen take the other path. Both warps contain a mixture of paths.

title: Group the signs
caption: In the grouped case, the first warp has only negative inputs and the second has only positive inputs. Timing depends on the compiled instructions and work on each path.

title: Each token selects a counter
caption: Each thread reads a token and atomically increments its selected counter. In this case all thirty-two tokens select counter two.

title: Predict the final count
caption: All counters start at zero. What will counter two contain after all thirty-two updates?

title: Atomic updates count every token
caption: Counter two contains thirty-two. Every atomic update is counted.

title: Why an ordinary increment can lose a count
caption: With an ordinary increment, two threads could both read zero and both write one. Two increments would leave a count of one.

caption: The block loads the seven keep flags into shared memory. Lane six begins with one, and the extra slot contains zero.

title: Predict the last running total

caption: The inclusive total at index six is four. Since destinations start at zero, the final kept item goes to position three.

caption: The two zero shifts have the same exponential, one. Dividing by the shared row sum gives those columns equal probabilities.
